facts.fact_text: On 30 March 2004 the second applicant and two other members of Ilinden notified the Mayor of Sandanski that the organisation intended to stage a rally on 18 April 2004.
The rally notified on 30 March 2004 was planned to take place between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on 18 April 2004 at the grave of Yane Sandanski near the Rozhen Monastery.
The planned rally notified on 30 March 2004 would include laying flowers at the grave of Yane Sandanski.
The planned rally notified on 30 March 2004 would include making speeches about the life and activity of Yane Sandanski.
The planned rally notified on 30 March 2004 would include a "cultural programme".
In the letter of 20 April 2004, the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that to proclaim Gotse Delchev a "Macedonian revolutionary" was "unconstitutional and provocative".
The Blagoevgrad District Court instructed Ilinden to provide proof of registration in connection with its application for judicial review filed on 26 April 2004.
On 23 August 2004 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to hold a rally at 3 p.m. on 12 September 2004 in front of Gotse Delchev's monument on Macedonia Square in Blagoevgrad.
The purpose of the rally notified on 23 August 2004 was to commemorate the Macedonians who fell victim to State terrorism and genocide in Bulgaria, by laying wreaths and making a short speech.
The rally took place on 4 May 2005.
On 5 October 2006 the Mayor of Sandanski confirmed that the hall would be in use on the requested date and stated that no other venue of such a size existed.

According to the applicants, at about 10.30 a.m. on 18 April 2004 a plain-clothes police officer, accompanied by two uniformed police officers, approached the organisers and told them to stop decorating the stage.

According to the applicants, the plain-clothes police officer told the organisers on 18 April 2004 that the Mayor's permission was valid only until 12 noon and that after that they were to leave the area.
According to the applicants, the police officer's statement on 18 April 2004 led to tension, with some of the participants reacting forcefully.
After the tension on 18 April 2004, the rally was allowed to proceed.

On 3 May 2004 the police, relying on section 62 of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered the head of Ilinden's Blagoevgrad chapter not to organise rallies by members of Ilinden without permission by the Mayor of Blagoevgrad and in breach of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act.

The police order of 3 May 2004 admonished the head of Ilinden's Blagoevgrad chapter to coordinate the members of Ilinden to prevent demonstrations with foreign flags and other symbols, or the display of placards with anti-Bulgarian slogans, which was likely to incite unrest and breaches of public order.

On 3 May 2004 the police ordered another member of Ilinden not to commemorate the anniversary of the death of Gotse Delchev or use propaganda materials against the Republic of Bulgaria and the Constitution of the Republic of Bulgaria.
On 12 September 2004 the members and supporters of Ilinden gathered in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad were surrounded by about twenty-five uniformed police officers.
On 12 September 2004 two plain-clothes police officers approached the leaders of the Ilinden rally and asked them to leave the placards and banners they were carrying.
On 12 September 2004 the participants in the Ilinden rally were surrounded by police, who apparently told them several times to put the flag and the placards down.
On 12 September 2004 about eighty metres from the monument to Gotse Delchev, a group of some forty police officers stopped the participants in the Ilinden rally.
At about 1 p.m. on 12 September 2005 members and supporters of Ilinden started gathering in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad with a view to marching to Macedonia Square.

On 12 September 2005 approximately thirty uniformed and plain-clothes police officers surrounded the Ilinden members and supporters gathered in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad, blocked their way, seized the flags and placards they were carrying, and destroyed a wreath.
According to the Government, the actions of the police on 12 September 2005 were monitored by a public prosecutor, who did not note any abuse of their powers.
At about 12 noon on 23 April 2006 the police interrupted the Ilinden gathering, telling the participants that the time allowed by the Mayor of Sandanski had expired and they should disperse.

In a letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad informed Ilinden that every citizen of the Republic of Bulgaria had the right to pay his respects to the memory of national heroes and lay flowers at their monuments.
In the letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the holding of rallies presupposed registration, proof of which Ilinden had not presented.
The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 8 September 2006 that the holding of a school holiday prevented the parallel holding of Ilinden's rally on 12 September 2006.
On 27 September 2006 Ilinden informed the Mayor of Sandanski that it had learned that the wrestling tournament would not take place and asked him to reconsider his decision.

On 26 March 2007 Ilinden informed the Mayor of Sandanski that UMO Ilinden – PIRIN would in fact be holding their event in the town of Melnik, in front of Yane Sandanski's monument, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., and that only a small delegation would go to the grave near the Rozhen Monastery to lay flowers between 10 and 11 a.m.
According to the applicants, on 29 July 2007 the Ilinden participants were stopped by the police before reaching Samuilova Krepost and were ordered to put the placards and banners down.
According to the applicants, the Ilinden participants obeyed the police order on 29 July 2007 and were allowed access to Samuilova Krepost without the materials.

The rally notified on 28 August 2007 was to mark the anniversary of "the genocide against the Macedonians" and would consist of the laying of a wreath and flowers on the monument and a short speech, lasting one hour.
The Blagoevgrad Administrative Court sent the file to the Blagoevgrad District Court in its decision of 30 August 2007.

According to the applicants, the arrested Ilinden members on 12 September 2007 were taken to a police station, held for about three hours, and charged with committing administrative offences for having tried to take part in a banned rally.

On 22 October 2007 the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad imposed administrative fines of 200 Bulgarian levs (102.26 euros) each on the second applicant and on a number of members of Ilinden for having taken part in a banned rally, in breach of a public-order regulation issued by the Blagoevgrad Municipal Council.
The second applicant and the members of Ilinden fined on 22 October 2007 all sought judicial review of the fines.
In a series of judgments delivered on 18 and 19 February, 11 March, and 22 and 29 May 2008 the Blagoevgrad District Court annulled the fines imposed on 22 October 2007.

In other judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court held that although the Mayor's ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2007 was legally binding, the actions of the members of Ilinden on that date had not amounted to the staging of a rally, as they had been too few and had not tried to wave banners and make speeches, but merely to lay flowers on Gotse Delchev's monument.

Section 12(1) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that where the time or the place of the meeting, or the itinerary of the march, would create a situation endangering public order or traffic safety, the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council, or the mayor, respectively, shall propose their modification.

Section 12(2) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council, or the mayor, shall be competent to prohibit the holding of a meeting, demonstration or march where reliable information exists that it aims at the violent overturning of constitutional public order or is directed against the territorial integrity of the country.

Section 12(2) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council, or the mayor, shall be competent to prohibit the holding of a meeting, demonstration or march where reliable information exists that it would endanger public order in the local community.

Section 12(2) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the President of the Executive Committee of the People's Council, or the mayor, shall be competent to prohibit the holding of a meeting, demonstration or march where reliable information exists that it would breach the rights and freedoms of others.
Section 12(3) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the prohibition shall be imposed by a written reasoned act not later than twenty-four hours following the notification.

Section 12(4) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the organiser of the meeting, demonstration or march may appeal to the Executive Committee of the People's Council against the prohibition, and the Executive Committee shall decide within twenty-four hours.

Section 12(5) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that where the Executive Committee of the People's Council has not decided within the time-limit, the march, demonstration or meeting may proceed.

Section 12(6) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that if the appeal is dismissed the dispute shall be referred to the relevant district court which shall decide within five days, and that court's decision shall be final.

The 1990 Meetings and Marches Act was adopted when the 1971 Constitution was in force, under which the executive local State authorities were the executive committees of the people's councils in each district.

The 1991 Constitution abolished the executive committees of the people's councils and established the post of mayor, elected by direct universal suffrage, as the "organ of the executive power in the municipality" under Article 139.
Under section 62(4) of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, orders issued by the police were binding unless they obviously imposed the commission of an offence.
Section 62(5) of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act provided that police orders, when issued in writing, were subject to judicial review.

Section 55(1), (4) and (5) of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, which superseded section 62 of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act on 1 May 2006, has almost identical wording and is currently in force.

The Blagoevgrad District Court stated in its decision of 8 September 2006 that it was inopportune to allow adults and children to gather at the same time and place, to concurrently stage a school event and a political one, as "the children's fragile minds should not be subjected to the political interventions and influences which would inevitably occur if the two events [were] allowed to proceed together".

The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 27 April 2007 that while the lack of registration did not amount to sufficient grounds to prohibit the rally, the risk that it could infringe the rights of others was enough to justify the ban.

The Sandanski District Court held in its decision of 17 April 2008 that the Mayor of Sandanski had not banned the rally but merely proposed a change in its timing, as was his duty under section 12(1) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act.
On 12 September 2008 the participants in the Ilinden rally headed towards Macedonia Square in Blagoevgrad.
On 12 September 2008 the members of Ilinden stood in front of Gotse Delchev's monument on Macedonia Square, laid a wreath and flowers, and lit candles.
The police did not interfere with the Ilinden event at Macedonia Square on 12 September 2008.
After the Ilinden event on 12 September 2008, the police arrested a member of Ilinden who was taking photographs, took his camera by force, and exposed the film in it.

At the police station on 4 May 2009, the second applicant and two other members of Ilinden were issued orders under section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act not to take part in the rally prohibited by the Mayor of Blagoevgrad.
On 4 May 2009 the police seized a wreath with a ribbon saying "To Gotse from UMO Ilinden" from the Ilinden members.
On 12 September 2009 the police seized from the Ilinden members a poster bearing the inscription "12.IX. Day of the genocide against the Macedonian people".
On 12 September 2009 the police seized from the Ilinden members a red flag bearing the inscription "Macedonia" and depicting the "Star of Vergina".
